terminal_name: Summit Matarbari FSRU vs. Summit Matarbari LNG Terminal
verdict: not a duplicate -- two genuinely distinct projects
note: VERDICT: distinct projects, not a duplicate. (1) Summit Matarbari FSRU (T100000131051) is Summit's FLOATING (FSRU) project -- Bangladesh's proposed 'third FSRU' overall, contracted as 'Summit LNG Terminal 2 Company Ltd' under Summit Oil and Shipping Co Ltd, 600 MMcf/d (~4.6 mtpa), proposed 2021 -> govt-approved 2023 -> Bangladesh interim government CANCELLED the deal 7 Oct 2024 (finalized by Petrobangla 14 Jan 2025), now under Supreme Court appeal (stay on re-tender granted March 2025). (2) Summit Matarbari LNG Terminal (T100001082545) is a SEPARATE, larger LAND-BASED/onshore terminal proposal -- sponsor Summit Power International Ltd, partnering with Japan's Sumitomo Corp and JERA, capacity 7.5 mtpa (with a mooted expansion to ~10.5 mtpa), proposed 2023, Summit targeting first-phase operations in 2029 (vs. the government's earlier hope of 2027). Different vessel type (floating vs. onshore), different capacity, different corporate sponsor entity, different timeline, and independently reported as separate initiatives by multiple outlets with clear dates. CAVEAT worth flagging to the researcher (not resolved in this QC pass, out of the 5-row sample): the onshore side is genuinely crowded -- there is ALSO a Petrobangla-subsidiary (RPGCL)-led, state-tendered 7.5 mtpa land-based Matarbari terminal (GEM's separate 'Matarbari LNG Terminal' entity per gem.wiki), whose bidder shortlist was likewise reset by the interim government in Oct 2024 and which was revived in 2025 with a completed Tokyo Gas feasibility study. The in-brief ResearcherNotesProject note ('this project was originally the revised proposal within RPGC Matarbari LNG Terminal... now split out into its own proposal') confirms Summit Matarbari LNG Terminal's GEM record was carved out of that RPGCL-led terminal's history.
